definition: The AI Memos are a series of influential memorandums and technical reports published by the MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (MIT AI Lab), Massachusetts Institute of Technology, United States.
details: They cover Artificial Intelligence, a field of computer science.

explainer.lead: The AI Memos are a numbered series of research memorandums and technical reports from MIT’s AI Lab. They preserve important early work on artificial intelligence, programming languages, compilers, and computer chess, making them valuable both as technical references and as records of how those ideas developed.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a research lab keeping a numbered shelf of notebooks, with each notebook explaining a clever new experiment or invention. MIT’s AI Memos worked like that for ideas such as teaching computers to play chess and building the Scheme programming language. Reading them lets people revisit the original explanations rather than only hearing about the results later.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer can read individual memos for historical implementations and design arguments in areas such as Lisp, Scheme, interpreters, and compilers. AI Memo 39 covers a self-hosting Lisp 1.5 compiler, while the Lambda Papers trace Scheme-related work through interpreters, compilation, and processor design. These are numbered historical reports rather than a software package or current specification, so their notation and technical context should be checked against modern tools before reuse.
tiers.paperLevel: The AI Memos are a series of memorandums and technical reports published by the MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, with individual entries identified by memo or report number. Notable works include AI Memo 239, HAKMEM (1972), a compendium of hacks and algorithms, and Sussman and Steele’s Lambda Papers, including AI Memo 349 on Scheme (1975) and AI Technical Report 474 on the RABBIT Scheme compiler (1978). The series is a publication collection, not a single algorithm, formal model, or unified research method.

explainer.example: A programmer studying Scheme could begin with AI Memo 349, “Scheme: An Interpreter for Extended Lambda Calculus” (1975), then follow the later Lambda Papers through procedure-call implementation and AI Technical Report 474, “RABBIT: A Compiler for SCHEME” (1978). This provides a concrete trail from an interpreter to later implementation work.

usedIn.name: Programming-language research
usedIn.detail: The Lambda Papers document interpreters, procedure calls, and other ideas connected with Scheme.

usedIn.name: Compiler construction
usedIn.detail: Reports describe a self-hosting Lisp 1.5 compiler and the RABBIT compiler for Scheme.

usedIn.name: Computer chess
usedIn.detail: AI Memo 41 describes Kotok-McCarthy, an early program that played chess convincingly.

usedIn.name: Algorithms and programming techniques
usedIn.detail: HAKMEM collects a wide range of hacks and algorithms in AI Memo 239.

explainer.intuition: The series is best understood as a numbered research notebook for MIT’s AI Lab: each entry records a particular investigation, implementation, or collection of techniques. Its influence comes from the individual works it contains, not from one shared theory across every memo.
howItWorks: Researchers at MIT’s AI Lab wrote memorandums or technical reports on particular topics.
Each work received an identifying number, such as AI Memo 239 or AI Technical Report 474.
An entry could describe a program, explain a language implementation, present design arguments, or collect algorithms.
Readers use the number and title to identify a specific work within the broader series.
explainer.whyItMatters: The memos document influential work close to its original technical setting, including HAKMEM, Kotok-McCarthy, and the Lambda Papers. They therefore connect artificial-intelligence history with practical developments in chess programs, interpreters, compilers, and Lisp-based processors.
misconceptions: An AI Memo is not necessarily a short informal note; the series also includes substantial technical reports.
The memos are not all about machine learning or one common AI method; the listed works span compilers, chess, algorithms, Scheme, and processors.
HAKMEM and the Lambda Papers are specific works within the series, not alternative names for the entire collection.

diagram.caption: The AI Memos are a publication series whose notable entries cover several distinct technical topics.
